Biogeochemistry (2022) 160:211–229
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10533-022-00956-2

Soil carbon accumulation after afforestation of former croplands

Anna Müller · Piotr Kowalski

Received: 1 March 2022 / Accepted: 2 August 2022 / Published online: 14 September 2022

Abstract Afforestation is promoted as a climate solution, but soil carbon gains are uncertain. We sampled 86 paired forest and cropland sites across Central Europe. Topsoil carbon increased by 0.4 Mg per hectare per year during the first three decades, while subsoil carbon did not change.

Keywords Afforestation · Soil organic carbon

Introduction

Summary statistics of earlier studies vary widely, and this sentence must not be taken as an abstract.

Conclusion

Afforestation of croplands increases topsoil carbon steadily for at least thirty years. Subsoil carbon should not be counted in carbon credits without direct measurements.
